rule: L-2026-10-21-14 — a ruling names WHICH RUNG was unavailable and why; a rung that is merely HARD is not a reason. This instrument measures each rung over the whole admitted population.

grammar.citationRule: L-2026-10-21-20 — the sha256 of the bytes the REGISTRY SERVES. Never a path, never a log line.

population.rule: git ls-files per repository, 1 MiB cap

r1.sourceNote: the fetched source is the npm registry's own tree-sitter-javascript@latest grammar.js; the SOURCE is the question, because the source is what says whether the construct can exist in the grammar at all — a construct the source cannot spell is a construct no build of it can carry
r1.tokenOccurrenceNote: 'part' occurrences in the 0.25.0 source are `exponentPart`/`decimalPart` — a NUMERIC LITERAL helper, not a part directive; the count is reported with the sites it names

r2.question: could the construct be ADDED to the grammar source and then built (R2), and if so what would the patched grammar have to MATCH? The measurement is the population's own sites of the construct, because a patched grammar that can parse a spelling the corpus never uses still has nothing to publish.

implements.note: JavaScript's own language has no conformance clause. `class A implements B {}` is TypeScript, not JavaScript, and the corpus's class heritage carries ONLY `extends` — measured: 0 heritage children of any implements shape over the whole admitted population. A patched grammar could ADD an implements_clause, and it would then match nothing, because the construct is not in the language.

part_of.note: JavaScript has no part directive. The nearest construct in the language is the ES module import/export, which names ANOTHER MODULE — and that relation is ALREADY PUBLISHED under the `imports` label, so a `part_of` row would duplicate it under a second name.

r3.question: is there a node type the SHIPPED grammar ALREADY has that can carry the relation (R3)? The measurement is the served bytes' own inventory, read from the live language.

implements.note: the inventory is of the SERVED BYTES (63812b9e), not of the npm package's node-types.json, which is a DIFFERENT artifact and carries a different number

part_of.note: the node types that match /part/ are the ones whose NAME contains it — the question is whether any of them is a PART DIRECTIVE, and the corpus half measures the directive sites directly
